THE DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT, RUN 2026-08-31 ON ANTHONY'S WORD, and it returns "nothing here" — which the optimize skill explicitly permits as a successful outcome.

THE HYPOTHESIS UNDER TEST: that behaviour smeared onto the shared `DesignGraph` struct causes change fragility, so splitting the struct would reduce rebuild cost. THE EXPERIMENT DESIGNED TO FALSIFY IT: touch a LEAF module (granularity.rs, one impl block) and touch the GOD-STRUCT (graph.rs, 54 public methods on the shared struct), and compare. If the struct is the cause, the second must cost more.

═══ MEASURED, debug profile, two runs per condition, crates-compiled verified from cargo's own output ═══
                              workspace          core only     crates built
    no-op                  0.38s / 0.31s              —             0
    touch LEAF module     13.74s / 13.80s   4.39s / 3.93s        2 / 1
    touch GOD-STRUCT      13.80s / 14.09s   3.98s / 3.95s        2 / 1

⭐⭐ THE HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED. Leaf and god-struct are INDISTINGUISHABLE — the spread WITHIN a condition (13.74-14.09) is as wide as the spread BETWEEN them, and core-only is if anything marginally faster for the god-struct. Touching one impl block costs exactly what touching fifty-four costs, because the CRATE is Rust's compilation unit and both files live in `reflow2-core`.

⇒ A STRUCT SPLIT WOULD SAVE ZERO BUILD TIME. That is now measured rather than argued, and it closes the compile-fragility branch of the restructure question. `fact:change-fragility-is-crate-scoped-not-struct-scoped` reasoned this from Rust's compilation model; this measures it.

═══ AND WHAT A CRATE SPLIT WOULD BUY IS ALSO BOUNDED, IN THE SAME NUMBERS ═══
The whole 88-module `reflow2-core` crate rebuilds in ~4 SECONDS. So splitting core into N crates has a CEILING of about four seconds per incremental build, before counting the dependent chain that would still rebuild. That is not a restructure that pays for itself.

⭐ THE DOMINANT COST IS SOMEWHERE ELSE ENTIRELY, and the measurement hands it over unasked: core-only is ~4s and workspace is ~14s, so ROUGHLY TEN OF THE FOURTEEN SECONDS IS `reflow2-mcp` REBUILDING because it depends on core. The existing crate boundary is already earning its keep — it saves those ten seconds whenever only core is needed — and the largest single lever on incremental build time is the core→mcp dependency, not anything inside core.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ═══
· DEBUG PROFILE ONLY, one machine, warm cache. Release builds and cold builds are not measured and would be much larger; users get release binaries, developers get this.
· IT MEASURES ONLY BUILD TIME. The other three consequences of behaviour smearing — global coupling, write contention on the single RwLock, and per-module measurability — are untouched by this result and remain live arguments for a struct split. THIS KILLS ONE ARGUMENT, NOT THE PROPOSAL.
· It does not measure `cargo test` or `cargo check`, which are what a developer actually waits on most often; only `cargo build` was timed.
· No budget was written before this, because none was needed: the optimize skill's step 1 is measurement, and the answer arrived before any target was called for. Nothing was optimised and nothing should be.
